//: For your editor, not for a build: `grim-indexer build` compiles theme/**
through its own Astro config and never reads this file. It exists so that
`import CommandField from "@grim/components/CommandField.astro"` resolves
while you are writing the page, instead of showing as a missing module.
`@grim/*` is the renderer's own Astro source tree. Anything you import
from it you can also REPLACE, by putting a file of the same path under
theme/ - theme/components/CommandField.astro wins over the shipped one.
Page routes and this specifier are contract; component paths and props
are not yet, so pin the indexer version if you override one. The three
tiers in full are in theme/README.md.
`module` and `moduleResolution` are set rather than left to default,
because the default is not neutral: an unset `module` implies CommonJS,
and CommonJS implies `node10` resolution - deprecated on TypeScript 6
(TS5107) and hard-removed in 7, so a TypeScript bump you made for an
unrelated reason stops this file loading. The pair below is what actually
reads these specifiers: Vite, inside the renderer's Astro build. Nothing
here is ever emitted - `noEmit` says so rather than leaving it to who
runs it, or `tsc -p .` drops a theme/x.js beside every theme/x.ts - so
`bundler` costs no `.js` import extensions.
No `baseUrl`: it is TS5101-deprecated on TypeScript 6 and removed in 7,
and the `paths` target below resolves against this file's own directory
without it.
Deliberately self-contained - no `extends`. This file sits above the
directory the renderer builds in, so a tsconfig that cannot be PARSED
breaks the build rather than the editor, and an `extends` pointing into
node_modules cannot be parsed until npm install has run. Adding one
after that works; adding one before is a build that fails with an error
naming preact, not this file.
